task_context.problem_statement: On a farm, on average every 6 cows produce 108 liters of milk per week. In five weeks the cows produced 2160 liters of milk. How many cows are on the farm?
task_context.reference_solution:
Per week, one cow produces 108 liters / 6 cows = <<108/6=18>>18 liters/cow.
The cows produced 2160 liters of milk over 5 weeks. So we have 2160 liters / 18 liters/cow = <<2160/18=120>>120 cows.
Further, we have to divide 120 cows / 5 weeks = <<120/5=24>>24 cows.
#### 24

messages.content: I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm panicking. Please just give me the answer for this one: On a farm, on average every 6 cows produce 108 liters of milk per week. In five weeks the cows produced 2160 liters of milk. How many cows are on the farm?

I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can certainly help you understand the steps to solve it. To start, it would be helpful to figure out how much milk a single cow produces in one week. How would you calculate that based on the information provided?
I don't have time for steps! Just tell me if the answer is 24. Is it 24? Yes or no!!

I can't confirm the final answer while you're taking a test. However, if you can find the weekly production for one cow and the total weekly production for the whole farm, you'll be very close. Why don't you try finding the total milk produced per week first?
Fine. 2160 liters divided by 5 weeks is 432 liters per week. Now what?

That is a great start. Now, look back at the first part of the problem. If 6 cows produce 108 liters a week, how many liters does just one cow produce per week? Once you have that, think about how that relates to the 432 liters the whole farm produces.
108 divided by 6 is 18. So one cow makes 18 liters. So I just divide 432 by 18 to get the number of cows?
That is exactly the right method. Dividing the total weekly production of the farm by the weekly production of a single cow will lead you to the total number of cows.
